The Coffin of the Gods once slaughtered deities.
Then it chose a boy.
“I’m not good at saving lives,” he said.“But I’m excellent at ending them.”

Chapter 1
In Calebton, the capital of Zidonia…

"Hey, look! Isn't that Caleb Crawford?!"

"Whoa, it really is him!"

"He went missing a year ago, and his soul lamp went dark. The Crawford clan had been in an uproar because they all thought he was dead!"

"Exactly! I even heard that he ended up in Gehenna by mistake!"

"Oof! Gehenna?! That's supposed to be a place where all things go to die, and there's no escape!"

"Wait, then why is he here? Is he a ghost?!"

"No, he's not. And haven't you noticed? There's no Reiki in him at all. Could that mean he's lost his cultivation?!"

The countless students at Zoro Academy were in an uproar, gasping in shock as a tall, slender youth with a cool visage quietly entered.

And judging from his presence, he really had no detectable cultivation!

Soon after he showed up, news of his absent cultivation spread like wildfire and left the entire academy abuzz.

Everyone quickly rushed over for a look and saw that it really was Caleb as the rumors claimed.

He was the prodigy who had reached Ether in cultivation at only twenty, meaning that he already measured up to the clan elders who were a couple of centuries old. 

The Lord of Zoronda even honored him with the alias Caleb, and his future was endlessly bright, eclipsing the rest of the young potentials across the nation.

But suddenly, he went missing for no reason, his soul lamp turning dark, and he was presumed to be dead.

And yet, he had now returned!

"A year… Or a hundred?" Caleb mused to himself as he continued inside the academy at a steady pace.

His gaze drifted quietly about, yet his eyes carried an ancient depth that did not belong to a man of only twenty-one.

That was when a tall, curvaceous girl appeared right in front of him.

Her face was breathtakingly beautiful, with every little gesture and facial expression capturing the soul.

Seeing her, Caleb made a beeline for her, while everyone around them grew restless.

"Isn't that Zoronda's most beautiful woman, Delilah Gosling? Tut, tut… Caleb's quite the Romeo, isn't he, coming straight to her as soon as he's back?"

"Of course! Back in the day, he had so many girls obsessing over him, but he was only loyal to Delilah, always doting on her and tending to her every need."

"I even heard that he had showered her with Nature's boon. He's really spoiled her rotten."

As everyone kept talking, Caleb had reached Delilah.

"C-Caleb… You're alive?" she blurted in surprise, a million different thoughts crossing her mind, and it showed on her face.

However, she soon sensed that Caleb had lost all his cultivation.

Disappointment and contempt showed in her eyes, followed by relief.

"Well, it's good to have you back. Even if you've lost your cultivation, I'm sure your clan will still regard you with importance, so you can lead a worry-free life as the heir to your clan."

Looking into Caleb's dark stellar eyes, she then continued, "But let's just go our separate ways. We're never getting back together."

"Oh, to think that the prodigy a year ago is now reduced to a loser! It's just so poetic!"

The girl beside Delilah, who was just as beautiful, laughed derisively then, disdain and glee clear in her eyes. "Delilah is now Earthen rank one. You don't deserve her anymore!"

It was Delilah's best friend, Susie Larkin.

"Stop it, Susie."

Delilah glanced at her, and then turned back to see that Caleb remained cool and quiet. 

Still, she couldn't help putting up a lofty expression and leering at Caleb as if he were just an insect.

"Are you listening, Caleb?" she demanded. "Don't bother me ever again—there's nothing tying us together anymore. As for our engagement, it should've been annulled when your soul lamp darkened a year ago. But since you're back, we can have it formally annulled at my home." 

With those words, she took Susie's hand, ready to turn and leave, refusing to look at Caleb twice now that he was a loser.

"Wait."

That was when Caleb finally broke his silence.

Susie wheeled on him right then, snapping haughtily at Caleb, "What? What else do you want?! Give up already—Delilah is now beyond your reach!"

Everyone was buzzing right then.

"Shit, I didn't think that Delilah was that cold. I mean, can't she at least let the man talk?"

"You don't get it, do you? I heard that one of the heirs from the Sanctuary's Big Four clans has taken a liking to her. It's only natural that she's seizing better prospects."

"Tut, tut. Well, that was unexpected! Back then, Caleb always did whatever she asked, like giving her herbs, pills, spirit stones, and enchanted weapons, just so that she could advance through the ranks in the academy."

"Tut, tut. Is this what they call being used like a tool?"

Delilah cringed under the voices around her, but she soon composed herself.

In this world, might made right!

And a man without might was nothing—there was no value in him for her to keep him around!

Even as the thought crossed his mind, Caleb's cool words rang in her ear. "Regarding the engagement you were talking about… I'll personally visit your clan in three days and annul it!"

"W-What?!" Delilah turned, taken aback and wondering for a moment if she had heard Caleb wrong.

In her mind, Caleb would cling to her as he always did in the past and not agree to it so calmly!

But even as she was left stunned, Caleb continued, "Actually, the reason I came to you first thing after I've returned isn't to recount the good old days. Instead, I'm here to take back the dimensional ring that I gave you previously."

As he spoke, his impassive gaze was trained on Delilah's swords and all the enchanted jewelry she wore, especially the black ring on her finger. It was the dimensional ring, which was the only thing his mother had left him.

"Now that our engagement is annulled, it's only natural that all the gifts given as part of the engagement should be returned. That includes the Sky-Grade Snow Maiden Sword, the Earth-Grade Snow Robe, the Vorpal Bangle, the Ice Soul Necklace…"

There was a deathly silence as Caleb listed every gift he had given Delilah.

Everyone's jaws were hanging open, their eyes wide in complete disbelief.

Nonetheless, Caleb kept going and only paused when he finished. "And there's also the three million spirit stones that I'd given your father as an early dowry. I hope he'll have it ready when I visit in three days!"

His expression serene, he then held out his palm. "Let's start with what you're wearing and my mother's dimensional ring. Please return them."

Everyone remained silent, watching the pair in shock.

Delilah's ample bosom was heaving as she glared at Caleb, rage flaring from her heart and spreading throughout the rest of her.

Inside, she was screaming.

Everything belonged to her! 

He had given them to her, so they were now hers!

He had no right to take any of it back!

"Watch it, Caleb!" Susie snapped before Delilah could say a word. "Do you call yourself a man? You're taking back the things you've given? What a bitch!"

Caleb shot her a cold glance. 

“This doesn’t concern you,” he said flatly. “Say another word, and I’ll make sure you never speak again.”

Chapter 2
Caleb's glare left Susie feeling like a terrifying beast was watching her, leaving her cringing in fear and hiding behind Delilah.

Even though Caleb only used to be Zoronda's most powerful freak, Susie was still intimidated.

Still, she soon remembered that he was a loser now. Why did she have to fear him? What a joke!

Delilah was scowling too, and her fingers clenched tightly around the sword that gleamed in blue radiance.

Just feeling the potent Reiki ripples unfurling from it left her unable to part with it.

And then there was Caleb's dimensional ring that could carry even living objects… Her heart definitely bled over losing something so extraordinary!

Grief showing all over her face, she snapped at Caleb, "How could you be so despicable? Taking back what you gave me? What was it you said? That you'd love me forever, and you'd never hurt me or make me sad? Just look at what you're doing now!"

She was definitely reluctant to return Caleb's gifts when each was so precious and valuable.

That was especially the case for the black ring and the Snow Maiden Sword, which she really needed for the Derby in two weeks.

Held at the academy, even Sanctuarians would be attending the Derby.

And that meant it was Delilah's only ticket to Sanctuary, which was why she needed the Snow Maiden Sword all the more!

It was a sky-grade weapon, and even clan elders across Zoronda yearned for something like that.

"Heh…"

Caleb chuckled calmly. "Weren't you saying you wanted us to go our separate ways? Everything I listed belongs to me and bears my family crest."

His eyes narrowing, his voice turned cool as he continued, "This is neither a joke nor a discussion. Return everything to me, or the Goldings will be an enemy of the Crawfords, and we won't rest until you're destroyed!"

As they finished, the crowd around them was left abuzz as they gaped at Caleb in shock.

"Woah…"

"Gosh, Caleb wouldn't even have dared raise his voice around Delilah a year ago. Is that man still really Caleb?"

"Tut, tut. Talk about charisma… 'We won't rest until you're destroyed'? Let's see if the Goldings are brave enough to stand their ground against the Crawfords!"

"The Goldings? Really? You know that the Crawfords are one of the strongest families in Zoronda. Their might is there for all to see!"

"I mean, if the engagement is going to be annulled, it's perfectly reasonable to return the presents too, right? To think that Delilah only cares to receive and refuses to return them. The audacity!"

Delilah's expression darkened as the crowd around them mocked her out loud, and her eyes darted everywhere while her knuckles turned pale from clenching on the Snow Maiden Sword. 

But since she had decided to dump Caleb anyway, Delilah decided to give up on vanity. She snorted and said, "Hah! You have no cultivation, and you can't even protect yourself, Caleb! Do you really think you're still the heir to the Crawfords, and that you still speak for them? You must be kidding!"

In her mind, now that Caleb had lost his cultivation, the Crawfords would definitely strip him off his position as heir, and the other clan members would also be conspiring to kill him!

And in Calebton, or perhaps even all of Zoronda, internal disputes within clans were simply commonplace!

That was when an icy voice barked, "Yes! Caleb Crawford still speaks for the Crawford clan!"

Even as Delilah shuddered, everyone turned to find a big man with thick, dark hair and a gruff demeanor striding toward the center. 

A boundless, imposing might seemed to extend from him as he walked.

Over dozens of youths were right behind him, and all of them hurried toward Caleb, bowing in salutation.

"Young Master!" 

"Young Master!"

There was no lie in their greeting or their excitement, and their presence certainly rocked the hall.

Even as the onlookers backed away in surprise, Caleb smiled at the middle-aged man leading them. "Greetings, Elder Jax."

Jax was the ninth elder of the Crawford clan, and the man was pumping his fist in excitement as he laughed. "Haha! Welcome back, Caleb! I know you wouldn't die that easily!"

Pausing, he then asked in concern, "By the way, where have you been? You were gone for a year. What happened?"

Caleb smiled. "It's a long story. Let's talk when we're home."

"Haha! Of course!"

Jax nodded repeatedly before turning to a scowling Delilah with a sharp glare and growling, "Girl, you will return all the gifts you've received since you're asking to annul the engagement. It is my demand as well—or are you going to refuse?"

Even as Delilah's face turned pale from Jax's menacing presence and scary glare and she stumbled backward, a middle-aged woman strode up, snapping, "Hah! To think that an Elder of the Crawford clan, and a Skylord-ranked one at that, would bully a young maiden! Is that all you can do?"

Seeing the woman, Delilah's face lit up as she found her confidence again and hurried over to bow to her. "Master Larkin!" 

"Mother," Susie called out as she hurried over to Ryona Larkin as well, abruptly feeling as if Jax's menacing presence had diminished.

However, Jax was not holding back despite Ryona's intervention, and he even snorted coolly. "Ah, so this is why little Delilah has become brazen that she would only take without giving back… She's been taught exactly that! Tut, tut… You learn something new every day!"

"Watch your mouth!" Ryona glared furiously at Jax. 

"Then shut up! This isn't any of your business!" Jax bellowed back tempestuously before turning at Delilah with a sinister glare. "Are you going to return the young master's possessions or not? If you refuse, I'll return home to rally every able-bodied clan member and wage war on your house!"

Everyone around them gasped audibly at Jax's threat, clearly thunderstruck.

Even if Caleb's earlier threat didn't mean anything, Jax's threat definitely did!

"My goodness… But that's Elder Jax for you. Such an impressive temper."

"Tut, tut. He's always been famous for being hot-tempered, murderous, and a master of the blade! Even the Lord of Zoronda has to show him due respect!"

"Oof. To think that Zoronda's prettiest face is actually that thick-skinned! She wants to annul her engagement while keeping all the presents given!"

"Exactly. Those cheeks are fair, but that heart is completely dark."

"That's right. She clearly wants to dump Caleb after he's lost his cultivation, so that she has a shot with that Sanctuarian heir. But then, she's also reluctant to part with Caleb's presents. What even is that mindset? It's just unseemly!"

In the end, Caleb used to be very polite since he was chasing after Delilah. Now that she had better prospects, even the guards were getting smugger.

"Heh."

Caleb sneered in contempt and suddenly narrowed his eyes as he kicked the guard in the chest!

Bang!!!

There was a loud crash like clapping thunder as the guard's chest erupted and he was sent flying, crashing violently into the front gates!

When he finally dropped to the ground, he lay motionless, his fate unknown.

Several other guards arrived, trembling at the sight before them.

Still, one of them hollered, "How dare you!!!" 

Caleb simply advanced inside the compound, growling, "Stay out of my way if you want to live. How dare mere lapdogs like you bark at me!"

Naturally, the guards were afraid to stop him, only watching him in fear while scurrying away.

Brax and Jax shared a smile and leisurely followed Caleb inside.

Nonetheless, the commotion soon reached the hall and Quinton's ears, with Quinton glowering all at once.

"Hmph!" He snorted. "The audacity of that brat… I shall discipline him for the Crawford clan!"

Even as he finished, a cool laugh rang from the doorway. "Oh, what a laugh. You think you have the right to discipline me?"

Watching as Caleb entered in an elegant white robe with good looks that could match the gods, Quinton snarled ferociously, "Kneel this instant, Caleb Crawford!"

Chapter 1
In Calebton, the capital of Zidonia…

"Hey, look! Isn't that Caleb Crawford?!"

"Whoa, it really is him!"

"He went missing a year ago, and his soul lamp went dark. The Crawford clan had been in an uproar because they all thought he was dead!"

"Exactly! I even heard that he ended up in Gehenna by mistake!"

"Oof! Gehenna?! That's supposed to be a place where all things go to die, and there's no escape!"

"Wait, then why is he here? Is he a ghost?!"

"No, he's not. And haven't you noticed? There's no Reiki in him at all. Could that mean he's lost his cultivation?!"

The countless students at Zoro Academy were in an uproar, gasping in shock as a tall, slender youth with a cool visage quietly entered.

And judging from his presence, he really had no detectable cultivation!

Soon after he showed up, news of his absent cultivation spread like wildfire and left the entire academy abuzz.

Everyone quickly rushed over for a look and saw that it really was Caleb as the rumors claimed.

He was the prodigy who had reached Ether in cultivation at only twenty, meaning that he already measured up to the clan elders who were a couple of centuries old. 

The Lord of Zoronda even honored him with the alias Caleb, and his future was endlessly bright, eclipsing the rest of the young potentials across the nation.

But suddenly, he went missing for no reason, his soul lamp turning dark, and he was presumed to be dead.

And yet, he had now returned!

"A year… Or a hundred?" Caleb mused to himself as he continued inside the academy at a steady pace.

His gaze drifted quietly about, yet his eyes carried an ancient depth that did not belong to a man of only twenty-one.

That was when a tall, curvaceous girl appeared right in front of him.

Her face was breathtakingly beautiful, with every little gesture and facial expression capturing the soul.

Seeing her, Caleb made a beeline for her, while everyone around them grew restless.

"Isn't that Zoronda's most beautiful woman, Delilah Gosling? Tut, tut… Caleb's quite the Romeo, isn't he, coming straight to her as soon as he's back?"

"Of course! Back in the day, he had so many girls obsessing over him, but he was only loyal to Delilah, always doting on her and tending to her every need."

"I even heard that he had showered her with Nature's boon. He's really spoiled her rotten."

As everyone kept talking, Caleb had reached Delilah.

"C-Caleb… You're alive?" she blurted in surprise, a million different thoughts crossing her mind, and it showed on her face.

However, she soon sensed that Caleb had lost all his cultivation.

Disappointment and contempt showed in her eyes, followed by relief.

"Well, it's good to have you back. Even if you've lost your cultivation, I'm sure your clan will still regard you with importance, so you can lead a worry-free life as the heir to your clan."

Looking into Caleb's dark stellar eyes, she then continued, "But let's just go our separate ways. We're never getting back together."

"Oh, to think that the prodigy a year ago is now reduced to a loser! It's just so poetic!"

The girl beside Delilah, who was just as beautiful, laughed derisively then, disdain and glee clear in her eyes. "Delilah is now Earthen rank one. You don't deserve her anymore!"

It was Delilah's best friend, Susie Larkin.

"Stop it, Susie."

Delilah glanced at her, and then turned back to see that Caleb remained cool and quiet. 

Still, she couldn't help putting up a lofty expression and leering at Caleb as if he were just an insect.

"Are you listening, Caleb?" she demanded. "Don't bother me ever again—there's nothing tying us together anymore. As for our engagement, it should've been annulled when your soul lamp darkened a year ago. But since you're back, we can have it formally annulled at my home." 

With those words, she took Susie's hand, ready to turn and leave, refusing to look at Caleb twice now that he was a loser.

"Wait."

That was when Caleb finally broke his silence.

Susie wheeled on him right then, snapping haughtily at Caleb, "What? What else do you want?! Give up already—Delilah is now beyond your reach!"

Everyone was buzzing right then.

"Shit, I didn't think that Delilah was that cold. I mean, can't she at least let the man talk?"

"You don't get it, do you? I heard that one of the heirs from the Sanctuary's Big Four clans has taken a liking to her. It's only natural that she's seizing better prospects."

"Tut, tut. Well, that was unexpected! Back then, Caleb always did whatever she asked, like giving her herbs, pills, spirit stones, and enchanted weapons, just so that she could advance through the ranks in the academy."

"Tut, tut. Is this what they call being used like a tool?"

Delilah cringed under the voices around her, but she soon composed herself.

In this world, might made right!

And a man without might was nothing—there was no value in him for her to keep him around!

Even as the thought crossed his mind, Caleb's cool words rang in her ear. "Regarding the engagement you were talking about… I'll personally visit your clan in three days and annul it!"

"W-What?!" Delilah turned, taken aback and wondering for a moment if she had heard Caleb wrong.

In her mind, Caleb would cling to her as he always did in the past and not agree to it so calmly!

But even as she was left stunned, Caleb continued, "Actually, the reason I came to you first thing after I've returned isn't to recount the good old days. Instead, I'm here to take back the dimensional ring that I gave you previously."

As he spoke, his impassive gaze was trained on Delilah's swords and all the enchanted jewelry she wore, especially the black ring on her finger. It was the dimensional ring, which was the only thing his mother had left him.

"Now that our engagement is annulled, it's only natural that all the gifts given as part of the engagement should be returned. That includes the Sky-Grade Snow Maiden Sword, the Earth-Grade Snow Robe, the Vorpal Bangle, the Ice Soul Necklace…"

There was a deathly silence as Caleb listed every gift he had given Delilah.

Everyone's jaws were hanging open, their eyes wide in complete disbelief.

Nonetheless, Caleb kept going and only paused when he finished. "And there's also the three million spirit stones that I'd given your father as an early dowry. I hope he'll have it ready when I visit in three days!"

His expression serene, he then held out his palm. "Let's start with what you're wearing and my mother's dimensional ring. Please return them."

Everyone remained silent, watching the pair in shock.

Delilah's ample bosom was heaving as she glared at Caleb, rage flaring from her heart and spreading throughout the rest of her.

Inside, she was screaming.

Everything belonged to her! 

He had given them to her, so they were now hers!

He had no right to take any of it back!

"Watch it, Caleb!" Susie snapped before Delilah could say a word. "Do you call yourself a man? You're taking back the things you've given? What a bitch!"

Caleb shot her a cold glance. 

“This doesn’t concern you,” he said flatly. “Say another word, and I’ll make sure you never speak again.”

Chapter 2
Caleb's glare left Susie feeling like a terrifying beast was watching her, leaving her cringing in fear and hiding behind Delilah.

Even though Caleb only used to be Zoronda's most powerful freak, Susie was still intimidated.

Still, she soon remembered that he was a loser now. Why did she have to fear him? What a joke!

Delilah was scowling too, and her fingers clenched tightly around the sword that gleamed in blue radiance.

Just feeling the potent Reiki ripples unfurling from it left her unable to part with it.

And then there was Caleb's dimensional ring that could carry even living objects… Her heart definitely bled over losing something so extraordinary!

Grief showing all over her face, she snapped at Caleb, "How could you be so despicable? Taking back what you gave me? What was it you said? That you'd love me forever, and you'd never hurt me or make me sad? Just look at what you're doing now!"

She was definitely reluctant to return Caleb's gifts when each was so precious and valuable.

That was especially the case for the black ring and the Snow Maiden Sword, which she really needed for the Derby in two weeks.

Held at the academy, even Sanctuarians would be attending the Derby.

And that meant it was Delilah's only ticket to Sanctuary, which was why she needed the Snow Maiden Sword all the more!

It was a sky-grade weapon, and even clan elders across Zoronda yearned for something like that.

"Heh…"

Caleb chuckled calmly. "Weren't you saying you wanted us to go our separate ways? Everything I listed belongs to me and bears my family crest."

His eyes narrowing, his voice turned cool as he continued, "This is neither a joke nor a discussion. Return everything to me, or the Goldings will be an enemy of the Crawfords, and we won't rest until you're destroyed!"

As they finished, the crowd around them was left abuzz as they gaped at Caleb in shock.

"Woah…"

"Gosh, Caleb wouldn't even have dared raise his voice around Delilah a year ago. Is that man still really Caleb?"

"Tut, tut. Talk about charisma… 'We won't rest until you're destroyed'? Let's see if the Goldings are brave enough to stand their ground against the Crawfords!"

"The Goldings? Really? You know that the Crawfords are one of the strongest families in Zoronda. Their might is there for all to see!"

"I mean, if the engagement is going to be annulled, it's perfectly reasonable to return the presents too, right? To think that Delilah only cares to receive and refuses to return them. The audacity!"

Delilah's expression darkened as the crowd around them mocked her out loud, and her eyes darted everywhere while her knuckles turned pale from clenching on the Snow Maiden Sword. 

But since she had decided to dump Caleb anyway, Delilah decided to give up on vanity. She snorted and said, "Hah! You have no cultivation, and you can't even protect yourself, Caleb! Do you really think you're still the heir to the Crawfords, and that you still speak for them? You must be kidding!"

In her mind, now that Caleb had lost his cultivation, the Crawfords would definitely strip him off his position as heir, and the other clan members would also be conspiring to kill him!

And in Calebton, or perhaps even all of Zoronda, internal disputes within clans were simply commonplace!

That was when an icy voice barked, "Yes! Caleb Crawford still speaks for the Crawford clan!"

Even as Delilah shuddered, everyone turned to find a big man with thick, dark hair and a gruff demeanor striding toward the center. 

A boundless, imposing might seemed to extend from him as he walked.

Over dozens of youths were right behind him, and all of them hurried toward Caleb, bowing in salutation.

"Young Master!" 

"Young Master!"

There was no lie in their greeting or their excitement, and their presence certainly rocked the hall.

Even as the onlookers backed away in surprise, Caleb smiled at the middle-aged man leading them. "Greetings, Elder Jax."

Jax was the ninth elder of the Crawford clan, and the man was pumping his fist in excitement as he laughed. "Haha! Welcome back, Caleb! I know you wouldn't die that easily!"

Pausing, he then asked in concern, "By the way, where have you been? You were gone for a year. What happened?"

Caleb smiled. "It's a long story. Let's talk when we're home."

"Haha! Of course!"

Jax nodded repeatedly before turning to a scowling Delilah with a sharp glare and growling, "Girl, you will return all the gifts you've received since you're asking to annul the engagement. It is my demand as well—or are you going to refuse?"

Even as Delilah's face turned pale from Jax's menacing presence and scary glare and she stumbled backward, a middle-aged woman strode up, snapping, "Hah! To think that an Elder of the Crawford clan, and a Skylord-ranked one at that, would bully a young maiden! Is that all you can do?"

Seeing the woman, Delilah's face lit up as she found her confidence again and hurried over to bow to her. "Master Larkin!" 

"Mother," Susie called out as she hurried over to Ryona Larkin as well, abruptly feeling as if Jax's menacing presence had diminished.

However, Jax was not holding back despite Ryona's intervention, and he even snorted coolly. "Ah, so this is why little Delilah has become brazen that she would only take without giving back… She's been taught exactly that! Tut, tut… You learn something new every day!"

"Watch your mouth!" Ryona glared furiously at Jax. 

"Then shut up! This isn't any of your business!" Jax bellowed back tempestuously before turning at Delilah with a sinister glare. "Are you going to return the young master's possessions or not? If you refuse, I'll return home to rally every able-bodied clan member and wage war on your house!"

Everyone around them gasped audibly at Jax's threat, clearly thunderstruck.

Even if Caleb's earlier threat didn't mean anything, Jax's threat definitely did!

"My goodness… But that's Elder Jax for you. Such an impressive temper."

"Tut, tut. He's always been famous for being hot-tempered, murderous, and a master of the blade! Even the Lord of Zoronda has to show him due respect!"

"Oof. To think that Zoronda's prettiest face is actually that thick-skinned! She wants to annul her engagement while keeping all the presents given!"

"Exactly. Those cheeks are fair, but that heart is completely dark."

"That's right. She clearly wants to dump Caleb after he's lost his cultivation, so that she has a shot with that Sanctuarian heir. But then, she's also reluctant to part with Caleb's presents. What even is that mindset? It's just unseemly!"

Even as everyone clamored, Delilah scowled like she had swallowed a fly.

This wasn't what she expected!

A year ago, Celeb would have been begging her not to leave and keep showering her with gifts to cheer her up.

But now, he had changed!

She knew it—all men were pigs, always changing their minds! 

Despite all the sweet things Caleb had said to her before, he was now treating her like dirt anyway!

Even as indignation flared in her heart, her expression turned meek, miserable, and even helpless as tears welled up in her eyes.

However, instead of earning anyone's sympathy, everyone was ridiculing her even more.

"Gosh, did you see that?! She actually feels hurt?!"

"Whoa, her tears definitely earn her a lot of sympathy, but just remembering how heartless she was before sickens me!"

"Shit, and she's acting so aggrieved like Caleb's the one bullying her."

"Exactly. He even said it—he doesn't mind annulling their engagement, but she just has to return everything he gave her. It's that simple!"

"She probably wants to dump him but keep the goodies…"

The words of the onlooking crowd clawed at Delilah's nerves, and she really wanted to bury her head in the sand right then!

However, she soon mustered herself and threw the dimensional ring and the Snow Maiden Sword at Caleb.

Chapter 3
Even though Delilah's heart ached just watching the dimensional ring and the Snow Maiden Sword fly toward Caleb, she knew she couldn't take them back with so many people watching.

It upset her all the more that Jax was glaring at her like she owed him her life, and her own mentor didn't dare breathe a word with Jax's threat!

Delilah stamped her feet spitefully, but with Caleb staring at her pointedly, she had no choice but to take off the mystic items she was wearing and throw them at him, one after the other.

Each time she threw one it felt like a pound of flesh was sliced off her body—and she was absolutely reluctant.

Standing beside Delilah, Ryona could feel her pain, as she was Delilah's mentor and had also received some of the goodies Delilah had been siphoning off Caleb—Delilah always knew to share with her, after all.

When Delilah was done, she scowled at Caleb. "That's everything. Are we done?!"

However, Caleb was staring pointedly at her robes, but Delilah snapped furiously, "Don't you dare! Do you think I'd take off my robes right here, right now?!"

While the eyes of everyone around them lit up right then, Caleb's gaze was cool in comparison. "I'll give you three days. Tell your father to prepare the spirit stones, and I want the mystic robes back too when I come to annul our engagement!"

Delilah's eyes were red from grief, as Caleb spoke like he wasn't bothered to look at her twice.

"Hmph! Let's go, Susie!" She snorted coolly, taking Susie by the hand and storming off with Ryona.

Caleb watched them coolly as they left before turning and leaving with Jax and the other 
members of the Crawford clan.

When they were gone, everyone was left sighing at the end of the storm.

Meanwhile, Delilah was feeling a mess of different emotions as she left.

The more she thought about it, the more aggrieved she was. 

Her eyes burned as tears welled up, and she sniffed softly, "Heh, that man has really changed! He wouldn't have spoken to me like that a year ago!"

"Oh, Delilah, he was nothing good anyway!" Susie said indignantly. "All the stuff he gave was given over a year ago, and he has the cheek to demand you give them back? Oh, you really learn something new every day!

"Don't be sad about it—he doesn't deserve you even if he still had his cultivation! Wilbur Jormont is the better match for you in every way, as he's the child of an illustrious Sanctuary clan!"

Ryona nodded as she added coolly, "Susie's right. You're beautiful, and you have decent talent. It's both your triumph and your good fortune that you've caught Wilbur's eye. Who cares about Caleb Crawford anyway?!"

Delilah nodded slightly. 

She had been a little sad when she first heard that Caleb's soul lamp had darkened.

But before long, she realized she was just not used to one less person showering her with gifts and sucking up to her.

Then, a month ago, Wilbur came to Zoronda.

He was the youngest son of the Jormont clan, one of the Sanctuary's Big Four clans, who was allegedly visiting to select a young batch of apprentices and take them to the Sanctuary for training.

The news rocked Zoronda as soon as it spread, with all the star pupils of Zoro Academy organizing a Derby, which was meant to curry favor for the opportunity to go to the Sanctuary.

On top of that, Wilbur had already shown interest in Delilah and was wooing her…

The thought that she would make it to the Sanctuary already made her feel better, while she also assured herself that the goodies Wilbur would give her were definitely much better than anything Caleb could give.

Beside her, Susie's eyes twinkled as she hatched the perfect plan. "Come on, Delilah—let's talk to Wilbur and ask for his help! There's no reason we should just return Caleb's spirit stones to him.

"Heck, with Wilbur's help, we could make Caleb return the Snow Maiden Sword and all the other gifts he's taken back! He won't ever measure up to a prodigy from the Sanctuary, after all!"

Delilah's eyes lit up too, the gloom clouding her heart clearing in an instant.

"Thank goodness you're always here for me, Susie. I knew I could count on you." Delilah said solemnly and quickly said goodbye to Ryona before going to look for Wilbur.

-

In the hall of the Crawford residence…

As the top clan of Zoronda, the Crawfords' residence was huge, and the hall easily fit all the clan elders and apprentices without issue.

They were all excited about Caleb's return, with the clan chief, Xar Crawford, laughing heartily and clearly delighted to see Caleb. "Hahaha! As long as you know your way home, son! As the junior chief and a youth with the talent to reach the Emperor rank, there's no way you would fall that easily!"

Xar was clearly relieved, and judging from how everyone else was smiling cheerfully, they felt just the same.

Over the past year, they hadn't slept or eaten well as they kept searching for Caleb, and many had even died because of that.

In the end, the nine clan elders each had their own ideas in mind, and there was this mysterious twinkle in their eyes…

However, Caleb never noticed any of that, as he was earnestly touched by the warm, homely reception.

He was actually surprised the Crawfords were still treating him so well. He said solemnly, "Chief Xar, I've lost all my cultivation and am no longer suitable to be the junior chief. You should choose a new junior chief from the clan members."

The hall was suddenly silent as he finished.

Then, before Xar could speak, the black-clad woman beside him strode toward Caleb.

Her visage was flawless with a touch of iciness, and her sharp gaze had this apathy as if she were a mere observer of all existence.

As Caleb turned to her, he bowed his head respectfully. "Elder." 

She was the leading elder in the Crawford clan, and she had the appearance of a young woman. 

Behind her, a jet-black sword hovered over thin air, and Caleb's heart raced every time he saw it.

After all, it was the epitome of destruction and death.

"What are you saying, Cal? The position of junior chief is yours forever. No one has the right to  replace you."

The Crawford clan had nine elders, ranked from the First Elder to the Ninth, six men and three women, all of them immensely powerful.

"That's right!" Jax's voice boomed in the hall. "You lost your cultivation? Then start cultivating again! I doubt that we can't achieve that much if we invest the entire clan's resources in you!"

Lux Crawford, who was the sixth Crawford elder, smiled and nodded. "That's right! The honors and wealth that Caleb had claimed for our clan are more than what the rest of our younger generations could ever hope to achieve. That sets his claim as junior chief beyond question!"

His eyes were dark as the starry sky, as if he could see through the whole universe, and the occasional gleam in that gaze would leave anyone cringing in fear.

"I concur! Lux is right about that!" Eldin Crawford, the mild-mannered second Crawford elder, spoke up too. 

He was wearing a scholar's robe and had grown his beard out to chest length.

His cheeks were a healthy flush, and his dark gaze seemed to see the path of the divine.

His hair was slicked back with a wooden hair stick, and his robes were an elegant cloud print. Each thread and embroidery seemed to be transcendent, standing above mere mortality.

"Brother Caleb, don't try to convince us otherwise! None of us has what it takes to replace you. You're our junior chief even if you had no cultivation!" 

"That's right! You'll always be our junior chief, and we'll serve you for life!"

Dozens of juniors were agreeing all at once, making it very clear that none of them coveted Caleb's place as the heir.

Caleb couldn't help but feel touched, even as he looked around at everyone in the hall showing such solidarity.

Before he could speak, an elderly voice cut him short. "Cal, let's put the discussion of your inheritance aside. Why don't you tell us where you've been for the past year?"

Caleb turned toward the Fifth Elder.

The white-haired old man wore a gentle expression, a faint herbal scent clinging to him.
Caleb bowed his head.

“Yes, Elder Witz.”

Looking around at everyone's eager stares, he sighed. "I was in Gehenna."

Gehenna! 

Just as they thought! 

There was silence, but everyone didn't appear all that surprised, if just a little shocked.

Xar himself felt his heart skip a beat, his shock showing all over his face. "Gehenna, where millions of coffins lay and rot, its very air filled with a strange black smoke and the breath of demons… How did you manage to get inside such a forbidden place? And how did you then escape?"

Caleb pursed his lips, feeling a mess of different emotions. "I had no idea who got me in there, but I woke up in a coffin… And when I managed to get out, it's been a year."

Everyone traded glances, all of them clearly finding his tale extraordinary.

Caleb stayed in a coffin within Gehenna for a year… and survived?

Unbelievable!

Chapter 4
"Damn it!"

Xar clenched his knuckles, his eyes flashing with rage. "Find out which villain threw Caleb in Gehenna. Our clan will not rest until we consign them to oblivion!"

"Yeah!"

Everyone agreed, murderous intent flaring throughout the hall.

"Alright! Now that our junior chief has returned, I'm sure he needs his rest," a beautiful woman said mildly just then.

Her name was Skye and she was the third elder of the Crawford clan. Her beauty was otherworldly, her hair cascading like a waterfall while her eyes gleamed with a bright sheen.

But at that moment, there was something piercingly cold in her eyes.

The other elders quickly nodded with looks of concern. "Yes, Skye is right. Let the junior chief rest in his chambers!"

Under their concerned gazes, Caleb took his leave.

As he returned to his chambers, he locked the doors and sat in a meditative pose on his bed.

Then, he rolled up his right sleeve to reveal the red markings on his arm and quietly spoke the words, "The Coffin… of the Gods…"

At his words, an ancient bronze coffin appeared, its very presence bloody and blasphemous as it hovered before Caleb.

Caleb stared at it pensively.

A year ago, he was blindsided, his essence and meridians taken away before being thrown into Gehenna.

It was a godforsaken place covered in coffins, from rotten wooden coffins to even bronze coffins.

Somehow, Caleb survived and woke up, finding himself mobbed by countless evil spirits and walking skeletons.

He fought them over countless days and nights, eventually fleeing in exhaustion and hiding within one of the coffins.

What he didn't expect was to find a boundless cosmos within.

He stayed inside for a hundred years, but only one year had passed when he emerged.

His physical body had been melted down, pulverized, and then remolded, so his cultivation was naturally gone, and he had no choice but to start over.

Here, in the continent of Sacra, the cultivation ranks progressed as follows: 

Gold, Mystic, Earthen, Ether, Ether Lord, Scion, Ruler, Sage, Emperor, and finally Divine. 

Each major rank was further divided into ten sub-ranks.

With that in mind, Caleb glanced at the dimensional rings beside him, each containing a substantial portion of the Crawfords' wealth.

They were giving everything to Caleb to help him regain his cultivation as soon as possible, and one of the rings was returned from Delilah.

This particular dimensional ring was pure black with an ancient presence to it, and the pocket dimension inside was so massive that one could put living beings within.

Be that as it may, some of those beings might die before long.

Still, it was the only heirloom Caleb had inherited from his mother, and there were still a few hundred thousand spirit stones inside that he had given Delilah. Even after a year, there were still plenty left.

And thankfully, the pocket dimension was also protected with a ward that only opened once in a while.

Having stayed in isolation within the Coffin of the Gods for a hundred years, Caleb's temperament had been honed endlessly.

Remembering those moments with Delilah a century ago, he found his own behavior childish.

As for Delilah's true nature, he slowly grew all too familiar with it over the endless years he had spent in isolation.

Hence, when he emerged from the Coffin of the Gods and heard that the Crawfords had spent most of their fortune searching for him, he decided to ask Delilah to return those spirit stones to make up for it.

Never could he have expected that Delilah would immediately demand the annulment of their engagement, and it made him all the more sure of her true nature.

"I just hope you're not deceiving me, Coffin," he said quietly just then.

"Haha! Over the hundred years, I've melted and crushed your physical body, your cultivation hence fading. But with the Breath of Chaos, your physical form was remodeled. Then, with the Breath of Origins, your psyche and spiritual senses were remade.

"The blood of ancient evil gods now flows in your veins, while the black holes of infinity have become your meridian nexus! The stars are now your very tendons and bones… Such are the many elements that combined as one, to grant you the body of the Creator! Don't get dissatisfied with me now, brat!"

Even as the Coffin continued, the lid slowly opened, revealing the cosmos within.

Caleb was silent.

He had no idea if what the Coffin was saying was true, but now, he had no choice but to trust it!

His clan had such high hopes for him—it was only natural that he didn't want to let them down!

Hence, he poured everything into the coffin, from the hundred thousand spirit stones to the rest of the Crawfords' gifts.

Soon, the coffin echoed with words that would leave all beings shaken to the core.

"Within the Coffin of the Gods, devourer of the four seas and anchor of the eight continents, lies a universe of stars and constellations, and yet its fire consumes all eras and the heavens, ever ready to leave all life in cinders…"

Even Caleb was shocked by the mighty boast!

That was when the coffin rumbled from the inside, as ripples of energy unfurled.

Even Caleb's cheek twitched, and everything he had put into the coffin, ranging from weapons and pills to mystic items, was all rapidly melting.

Everything was then converted into raw energy in the shape of white mist, slowly floating into Caleb's mouth, consumed and infused into his meridian nexus, nourishing his entire body.

Whoosh!

His cultivation strengthened exponentially, leaping from a mortal form to enlightenment, reaching Gold rank one, Gold rank two, Gold rank three… and it kept climbing all the way to the Mystic rank!

Still, when he reached Mystic rank ten, he stopped.

He opened his eyes, his pupils flashing with the horrific glint of Chaos.

He had improved by twenty sub-ranks!

"Unbelievable…" he murmured in shock.

His mind had been honed in the hundred years he spent in the Coffin of the Gods, but he still felt shock at that moment!

That was when an ancient voice in the Coffin dissed, "Tut, tut! Reaching Mystic already pleases you this much? Such ignorance. If you want to improve quicker, you gotta take more lives!

"Bring their corpses or Nature's treasures, and I will refine everything into pure energy, which will then be given to you, so that you will grow rapidly. Anything with Reiki works."

Caleb was naturally delighted to hear that, but he soon became puzzled as he asked, "Why me, Coffin? What is it that you want from me?"

"Tut, tut. There are billions of coffins in Gehenna, but you still end up in me. That could well be destiny! You could even say that you're the Chosen One!"

Caleb became silent at that and didn't dwell on it.

At the moment, he was still too weak.

He would probably need to grow until he had what it took to learn this world's secrets!

In the hundred years he had spent in the Coffin of the Gods, the Coffin had described to him how big the world truly was, and it really broadened his horizons.

Hence, he sat down in a meditative pose to augment his cultivation.

-

While Caleb cultivated, the nine Crawford elders and Xar gathered in the central chambers of their residence.

Everyone was trading glances, but most of them were clearly relieved.

Eldin then smiled meaningfully as he quietly said, "Kid, it appears that the reincarnation technique was a flawless success. It's also embedded in our minds, automatically generating missions and the plan to mold the body of the Creator."

Chapter 5
If anyone outside the clan were there, they would've balked when they heard Eldin, the second Crawford elder, calling the clan chief 'kid'!

However, Xar took no notice and even laughed. "That fella beyond the stars has just sent word that this is Caleb's death… but also his blessing! We would've all lost our minds if we weren't told to wait for a year ahead of time—patience was never our strong suit."

Everyone nodded in satisfaction.

Soon, time and space seemed to blur for a moment, as if someone was meddling with something.

The Crawford elders' gaze seemed to blank out for a moment.

Then, as if their memories were sealed, the menacing auras in the room suddenly calmed as they were ordinary people again…

Looking around at everyone, Xar laughed coolly. "It seems that we've been too humble for a while that they are really making light of us. Starting now, whoever dares to play dirty or tries to bully the weak, provoking our junior chief, I say death to them, no matter who they are!"

"Yes!"

The nine Crawford elders nodded, their auras unfurling at that moment and distorting the air around them.

They really weren't Ether Lord-ranked as everyone thought they were, but instead…

Suddenly, Jax was chuckling in amusement as he said, "That reminds me—chief, our junior chief intends to visit the Goslings in three days to annul his engagement, but we've been informed that Wilbur Jormont is there too. So how should we deal with that prick?"

"How else?" Xar growled coolly. "Just do as the junior chief commands. If there's defiance, punch them until they submit!"

"Yes, chief!"

As everyone nodded, Jax stood up. "Brax and I will take this one. Let's meet the two Jormont elders and see what they've got!"

"Heh. Works for me!" Brax, the eighth elder, nodded and followed him.

He was mild-mannered, calm, and composed.

However, there was a sword covered in a cloth slung over his back, and there was a bladelike sharpness in his gaze.

Sighing contentedly, he said, "Chief, I must say that I'm surprised at how mature our junior chief has become after just a year. He understands that we had it hard, so he immediately went to Delilah and demanded that she return everything he gave her. I wouldn't have expected something like that from him in the past."

"That's true. Not bad, if I do say so myself." 

Xar nodded in agreement. "That said, we must look busy. Make him understand that it's in hardship when we must strive hard, so that he won't stay a playboy who keeps goofing off."

As he finished, all the elders all traded understanding smiles right then.

-

Meanwhile, at the Goslings' residence, the entire clan was going all out as they fawned over a certain youth named Wilbur Jormont.

He was seated at the main seat in the middle of the hall, watching haughtily at everything around him.

Hearing Delilah's tearful complaint, he snorted in disdain. "Don't worry, Delilah. If Caleb Crawford dares show up here in three days, I will make him prostrate himself and apologize to you!"

Hearing that, everyone in the hall breathed huge sighs in relief, with Quinton grinning fawningly. "Go on, Delilah! Thank Young Master Wilbur already. We'd be bullied by the Crawfords if not for him!"

"Yes, Dad." Delilah beamed as she curtseyed at Wilbur. "Thank you, Young Master Wilbur. I will never forget this debt."

"Hehe! Come on, Delilah. Don't be a stranger," Wilbur said mildly, his eyes narrowing as he strode up to Delilah, taking her hands in his. "Your problems are my problems! Anyone who bullies you would be bullying me!"

Beside Delilah, Susie smiled meaningfully as she nodded. "That's right, Delilah. Do you really not understand what Young Master Wilbur wants? Don't let him down now."

As Delilah lowered her gaze shyly in response, Wilbur was left antsy even as he watched, but he couldn't exactly reach for a kiss when there were so many others around them.

"Ahem… Haha! Susie's exactly right!" Quinton exclaimed in delight, seeing how flirty the pair were getting. "Young Master Wilbur, if you like, we can arrange for Delilah to be engaged to you once her engagement with Caleb is annulled!"

As everyone around her beamed happily  in response, Delilah pouted as she lowered her gaze further. "Please, Dad! Why would you say something like that out of the blue?!"

With that, she took Susie's hand and ran off in embarrassment.

Even as they left, Susie's eyes were glued to Wilbur's, clearly communicating something from a distance.

Nonetheless, the rest of the Goslings laughed heartily as they watched Delilah run off shyly.

Wilbur was smiling too, but it was a smile that didn't reach his eyes as he was scoffing inwardly.

Marry him? Dream on!

That said, he didn't mind fooling around a little, as it looked to him that Delilah's hymen was still intact.

'Oh, Caleb Crawford. Can't even do that much after all the things you did for her?

'What a joke!'

Despite what he thought, he instead said, "It'd be my honor if I can marry Lady Delilah. However, I insist on spending time with her, so that we can bond and grow a connection, and not make it an abrupt matrimony."

"Haha! Of course, of course!" Quinton laughed out loud, clearly in a great mood. "Young 'uns always like a little flirting, I understand."

Back then, the Goldings had gained so much assistance from the Crawfords that they rapidly established themselves in the capital.

Now that Delilah had secured an even better prospect, Quinton could only sigh emotionally.

He really had a wonderful daughter!

Wilbur smiled. "Very well. I shall go to Delilah now."

"Go ahead, Mr. Jormont!" Quinton smiled fawningly.

With that, Wilbur led the two gray-haired geezers out of the hall toward the rear of the residence.

Along the way, the elder beside him asked softly, "Sir, are you sure you want to marry Delilah? I don't think your father would agree. Moreover, she kept dropping hints for you to give her treasures… She really is quite the schemer."

Wilbur snorted in disdain while looking sideways at the elder.

"Hah! Marriage? That can wait until the sex!" 

Even as Wilbur scoffed, he continued walking ahead. "As for giving her gifts… Hell no! Wealth is for flaunting, not to be spent on women. Do you understand?"

The elder was taken aback but soon nodded. "You really are wise, sir."

"That said… Delilah's quite amusing."

Wilbur smirked in disdain. "Playing hard-to-get like she isn't sure if she wants me. Haha! Trying to get me hooked and to pay through my nose even before I tap that? Dream on! She isn't getting shit from me until I have a taste!"

He had plenty of women in Sanctuary, and he could tell what position Delilah wanted with just a little tap on the bottom!

-

Three days passed in the blink of an eye, and news of Caleb's return rocked Calebton as it spread through every corner of the city.

After all, he had been the most dazzling prodigy of his time, but he now returned with cultivation.

It was inevitable for countless prying eyes to turn toward the Crawfords, as many of them inevitably started scheming…
Chapter 6
Outside Caleb's chambers at the Crawfords' residence, Brax and Jax were bemused, their surprise clear in their eyes.

It was just strange that they couldn't sense anything, considering their abilities.

"That's strange. I can't sense Caleb's presence at all… Isn't he in his chambers?"

"No way. He's been in there for three days and gave us express orders not to disturb him."

-

Meanwhile, in the dark depths of the cosmos, a rainbow bridge extended across the stars over several light years.

And in the depths of the bridge was an ancient oval mirror, gleaming with an abundant divine might that seemed to lord over all things.

A shadow in the mirror observed the Crawfords and snorted coolly. "Those old gods from the Pantheon of Longevity are really playful, aren't they? Sealing the memories of a mere clone to play house? Tut, tut… How frivolous!"

Naturally, no one could hear the sentient voice within the mirror…

-

Meanwhile, in Caleb's chambers, Caleb had disappeared from the physical realm and was now floating in the middle of an infinite cosmos after entering the Coffin of the Gods.

Staying in his meditative sitting posture, his aura was burgeoning.

At the same time, a violent energy was flaring within his body, giving him the presence of an ancient behemoth.

"Phew…"

There was no telling how much time had passed when he slowly opened his eyes, breathing out a turbid puff of air.

"Demonic Blood!" he murmured, his eyes wide with excitement.

It was the blood that the Coffin of the Gods had infused him with!

Aside from that, he was taught a cultivation method and a sword technique known as the Blood God Order and the World Burial Sword respectively!

And amid the infinite stars, the Coffin's voice boomed with satisfaction. "Kid, you have been given Kaos' heirlooms… His blood, cultivation, and sword technique! I expect you will master all three in three years. Not bad!"

"Thank you, Coffin!" Caleb stood up, bowing his head reverently toward the nothingness.

He was still inside the Coffin of the Gods.

Although three days had passed outside, it had been three years in here!

And in these three years, he didn't just receive the legacy the Coffin provided, but he had also mastered his own clan's cultivation method.

It had certainly been rewarding!

"Hehe…"

The Coffin remained formless as he chuckled in response, his voice echoing from near and far all at once. "Now, listen closely—you need the Wheel of Time to activate the Time Bubble. On this occasion, we've completely exhausted all the energy from the Wheel of Time. You need to find more to activate another Time Bubble and train with time dilation again."

Hearing that, Caleb pursed his lips in disappointment.

After all, with the time dilation inside the Time Bubble, cultivating in here for three years only meant three days had passed in the world outside.

Soon, he noticed an inconsistency. "Coffin, if one hundred years here is a hundred days outside, why was it a full year that passed the last time?"

The Coffin replied, "Each Wheel of Time varies in the purity of the Time Lord's authority, and it's the difference in purity that results in different degrees of time dilation."
 
Caleb nodded in silence—it was a shame.

If he could train a hundred years here, only a year would've passed outside.

Didn’t that mean he’d be basically invincible?

It was a real shame that the one hundred years before was spent with a coffin remolding his physical body.

And now, three years had been spent restoring his cultivation and inheriting new legacies.

Still, he was soon excited again, as he committed the name 'Wheel of Time' to his memory.

His breathing turned rushed at the thought, and he bowed again. "I shall remember all your guidance, Coffin."

"Good. Now get out."

The dimensions twisted and a vortex formed, and Caleb stepped inside.

When the world around him straightened, he was once again in his chambers.

"Kaos…?"

Caleb was unfamiliar with the name, but he knew that it was the name of a superior being existing on a higher plane, and that the Coffin wasn't telling him everything.

Clenching his knuckles and feeling the explosive energy in him, he knew he had reached Ether rank five!

He didn't just regain his cultivation level from a year ago, but he had ascended all the way up to Ether rank five in the Coffin! 

And this version of him was completely different from how he had been a year ago!

His eyes flashing murderously, he growled icily, "Just you wait, whoever stole my essence and left me for dead in Gehenna! When I find out who you are, I will drain you dry of every last drop of blood… Phew!"

Taking a deep breath to compose himself, he then extended his senses and noticed the two presences outside.

He quickly went over to open the door, and bowed his head when he saw that it was Brax and Jax. "Elder Brax, Elder Jax."

Both Brax and Jax were dumbfounded, crying out at the same time, "Caleb… You've regained your cultivation!"

Caleb smiled. "All thanks to the family's wealth and treasures. I won't let the clan down after all they've given for me." 

Jax laughed heartily. "Hahaha! Great! One must expect nothing less of our junior chief!"

Brax was delighted too, smiling and nodding at Caleb.

Caleb nodded in turn and said, "Elder Brax, Elder Jax… Shall we visit the Goldings' residence?"

With their clan caught in the midst of a financial crisis, there was no time like the present to get those millions of spirit stones back.

"Okay!" Brax and Jax nodded with emotional smiles and followed him.

That was when Caleb heard the Coffin's voice in his mind. "Tut, tut… Your clan, the Crawfords? They really are quite something."

"Really? How so?" Caleb asked in curiosity, while sliding a peek to see that Jax looked clearly excited, while Brax remained calm and modest.

The Coffin laughed. "I've cast the Time Bubble for you twice and virtually lost all my senses, but this feeling can't be wrong. Every elder of your clan is definitely not Ether Lord-ranked as you claimed."

Caleb's heart skipped a beat. "Could they be Ascendent?"

Being Ascendent naturally meant reaching the three advanced ranks of Scion, Ruler, and Sage, and the very thought sent Caleb's heart racing.

Was his clan really that powerful?

"I can't say for sure, as this realm is quite strange as if something is suppressing it. Why don't you observe them yourself?"

Caleb extended his senses to study Jax and Brax just then, but they still felt like they were Ether Lord-ranked to him.

Still, he shrugged, having no intention to dwell on the issue—his elders being strong was a good thing and suited him just fine.

It would also be a deciding factor on how he should treat his clan, whether he should tighten his iron fist or otherwise!

-

Before long, Caleb, Jax, and Brax arrived before the gates of the Goldings' residence.

Looking at the guards standing in front of the gates, Caleb spoke coolly. "Caleb Crawford, junior chief of the Crawford clan, has arrived!"

The guards simply snickered in disdain and started gloating nonchalantly. "Oh, the loser of a junior chieftain, you mean? Just wait here. I'll announce your arrival… later."

"Yeah, our clan chief is with a very important guest at the moment. He will be right with you when he actually has time."

They made sure to put a lot of emphasis on the phrase 'a very important guest.'

In the end, Caleb used to be very polite since he was chasing after Delilah. Now that she had better prospects, even the guards were getting smugger.

"Heh."

Caleb sneered in contempt and suddenly narrowed his eyes as he kicked the guard in the chest!

Bang!!!

There was a loud crash like clapping thunder as the guard's chest erupted and he was sent flying, crashing violently into the front gates!

When he finally dropped to the ground, he lay motionless, his fate unknown.

Several other guards arrived, trembling at the sight before them.

Still, one of them hollered, "How dare you!!!" 

Caleb simply advanced inside the compound, growling, "Stay out of my way if you want to live. How dare mere lapdogs like you bark at me!"

Naturally, the guards were afraid to stop him, only watching him in fear while scurrying away.

Brax and Jax shared a smile and leisurely followed Caleb inside.

Nonetheless, the commotion soon reached the hall and Quinton's ears, with Quinton glowering all at once.

"Hmph!" He snorted. "The audacity of that brat… I shall discipline him for the Crawford clan!"

Even as he finished, a cool laugh rang from the doorway. "Oh, what a laugh. You think you have the right to discipline me?"

Watching as Caleb entered in an elegant white robe with good looks that could match the gods, Quinton snarled ferociously, "Kneel this instant, Caleb Crawford!"

I was fluent in eight languages, but only spoke Italian at work.
My coworkers called me the department's dead weight.
My supervisor dumped stacks of contracts on my desk and said, "Copy these. That's all you're good for."
I never corrected them.
Until a multimillion-dollar negotiation.
Our star German translator froze on the third clause.
The deal was about to fall apart.
I set down my coffee and stood up.
"Alpha Throne, give us five more minutes."
And I spoke fluent German.
That Alpha looked up. He stopped packing.
The entire conference room fell silent.
And the pen in my supervisor's hand hit the floor with a sharp clack.

I was fluent in eight languages - Italian, German, French, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Arabic, and Russian.

But for three years at Nocturne Pack Trading, my resume only claimed one: Italian.

The reason was simple. My father had been a diplomat for the High Council, my mother a simultaneous interpreter for pack summits. Growing up, we rotated through seven different pack territories, so picking up new tongues was as natural as shifting under the full moon.

They died five years ago. A rogue ambush on the border - official report called it a "hunting accident." I didn't want to show off my skills. I didn't want anyone digging into my past and offering pity like a scrap of raw meat.

I wanted to keep my head down. Junior translator. Base salary. Pay the rent on my cramped den. Feed my cat, Vivi.

Then came the annual pack gathering. Our Alpha, Kellan Penrose, stood on the dais and droned in English for ten minutes before switching to German.

"Next year, I'm giving a seventy percent raise to every wolf in this hall who speaks German."

Two hundred pack members clapped, none of them understanding a word.

I understood every syllable.

Sandra Hayes, head of the German translation team, sat beside me. Her ears perked when Kellan finished, and she nudged my shoulder. "Did you catch any of that, Jenna?"

I shook my head. "No. I don't speak German."

She snorted. "Makes sense. You only know Italian and pull twenty grand a year. Pity."

I said nothing.

Only six wolves on the German team - plus Alpha Penrose himself - would actually see that raise. I reminded myself it wasn't my territory.

My phone buzzed. My only friend, Talia, from Administration.

"Babe Jenna, you totally understood Alpha's German just now, right? Seventy percent! Why didn't you speak up?"

Talia had accidentally discovered I knew French last year when she caught me reading a novel in the breakroom. I'd sworn her to secrecy - a hard oath for her to keep.

"Let it go. I don't want attention," I texted back.

"What's wrong with you? That's seventy percent! You're on twenty grand - that bump would take you to thirty-four. Your heater barely works, and your den's freezing."

I walked toward the elevators. Kellan was already there, with our Beta, Colson Anderson. They chatted in German.

"Smart move," Colson said. "Only the German team caught it. You reward your core wolves while everyone else thinks you're blowing hot air."

Kellan chuckled. "If I'm going to make empty promises, I might as well do it with class. German gives me that global-pack flair."

Colson snorted. "A junior translator like Jenna isn't worth more than twenty grand anyway."

The elevator doors slid open. I stepped in behind them, face blank. They kept talking in German.

"Who's handling the Eastbridge Pack negotiation next week?" Colson asked.

"Sandra," Kellan said. "Her German's the best."

"I hear Eastbridge's Alpha, Garrett Throne, is a nightmare," Colson said. "When they partnered with Skyline Pack, he barked at their translator until she fled the conference room in tears."

"Sandra can handle it."

The elevator reached the lobby. I walked out first. Kellan called after me in English, "Jenna, drop off the proofread for last week's Italian contract tomorrow."

"Of course, Alpha Penrose," I said, not looking back.

The next day, I dropped the proofread on Kellan's desk. Thirty thousand words of Italian. I'd found and fixed forty-seven errors in the original translation - Sandra's work. My name wouldn't appear anywhere. It would just say "Proofread by Translation Department."

Sandra never knew I corrected her. She genuinely believed she was an expert.

I was heading back to my desk when Talia drifted over, nursing a cup of blood-berry tea.

"Babe Jenna, did you hear?"

"Hear what?"

"Sandra's leading the Eastbridge pitch next week."

"I heard."

"Do you know who Eastbridge's Alpha is?" Talia dropped her voice. "Garrett Throne. Thirty-two. Ranked ninety-eighth on the Wolf Wealth List last year. Rumor has it he's fluent in five pack-tongues and has a vicious temper. He supposedly fired Skyline Pack's entire translation team after one meeting."

"What does that have to do with me?"

"Don't you think Sandra is going to bomb?"

"If she bombs, it's not my problem."

Talia sighed. "You put up with too much."

She left. I opened my laptop and pulled up my daily task - a supplier quote in Spanish. Normally the Spanish team handled it, but Kieran Gant was sick today, so Colson dumped it on me.

"Jenna, didn't you take some Spanish in college? Just do your best."

In reality, I'd lived in the Wolfstead Pack territory for two years. I finished the translation in fifteen minutes, deliberately leaving two minor errors that didn't change the meaning. I needed the work to look like it came from someone who'd only taken a few undergrad classes.

Colson's reply came fast: "It's fine."

Fine was good enough.

Later that afternoon, Sandra stopped at my desk and dropped a stack of papers in front of me. "Jenna, organize these Italian files. I need to prep for Eastbridge next week."

I eyed the stack - roughly fifty pages of background on Eastbridge Pack, all in Italian. "This really isn't my job - "

"Why wouldn't it be?" She cut me off. "You work in Translation, and I'm your team leader. Got a problem with me assigning you work?"

She'd been promoted to team leader last month, in charge of Italian and German groups.

"Fine." I grabbed the files.

She took a few steps, then looked back. "Oh, right. Department huddle tomorrow on the Eastbridge coordination plan. You don't need to be there."

"I know."

"You only handle basic proofreading anyway. You wouldn't be put on a major project like this."

"I know."

She walked away.

My phone buzzed - Talia, with a string of angry emojis. "I heard that from the breakroom. Who does she think she is, talking to you like that?"

"I'm used to it," I texted back.

"Can't you just stand up for yourself?"

"Stand up, and then what? She's the team leader."

"If you showed them all the languages you actually know, she wouldn't even be qualified to manage you."

"I don't want to do that."

"What exactly are you afraid of, Babe Jenna?"

I stared at the screen, no answer forming. What was I afraid of?

Maybe I was terrified of standing out. Terrified someone would dig into my past, look at me with that awful pity, and whisper, "Oh, she's the diplomat's daughter. The one whose parents were torn apart by rogues."

When I got home that evening, Vivi - my cat - was waiting by the door. I scooped him up, and he yawned wide.

"Vivi, I fixed forty-seven of Sandra's mistakes today, and she doesn't even know."

He squirmed out of my arms and padded to his food bowl.

I opened the fridge. Two eggs and half a head of cabbage. Making twenty grand in this city meant after rent, utilities, and cat food, I had almost nothing left.

I whipped up a quick omelet and sat by the window to eat. My phone rang - an unfamiliar number.

"Hello, am I speaking to Ms. Jenna Caldwell?"

"Yes."

"My name is Davis Jones. I'm an attorney with Kensington Law Firm, representing the High Council's estate division. We need you to sign documents regarding the liquidation of your parents' overseas assets."

"I've already told you. I don't want any of it. Donate it all."

"Ms. Caldwell, your parents had an account in Zurich - "

"I don't want it." I cut him off. "Thank you, Mr. Jones, but please stop calling me."

I hung up.

Vivi hopped onto the table, tilted his head, and watched me with those golden cat eyes.

"Nothing important," I told him.

I turned off my phone.

Monday morning. The Translation Department held its weekly pack meeting.

I wasn't invited. But my desk sat flush against the conference room wall, and my wolf ears caught every word.

Sandra stood at the whiteboard, mapping out Eastbridge Pack's specs.

"Garrett is fluent in German and Italian. His Betas cover French and Japanese," she explained. "They're handling Arabic themselves. We're only responsible for German and Italian comms."

Colson nodded. "Confident you can handle this?"

"Of course." Sandra's tail practically wagged. "I studied in German territory for three years. A standard business negotiation is a breeze."

Sandra's German was passable. She could navigate a casual chat over coffee without embarrassing herself.

But I'd proofread her drafts. Her business German was a disaster. She translated word-for-word, completely ignoring the rigid hierarchy of formal titles - something every German wolf expected in corporate correspondence.

In a casual setting? Fine.

Across the table from a detail-obsessed Alpha like Throne?

Whatever. Not my problem.

The meeting ended. Sandra passed my desk.

"Did you finish organizing those files?"

"Yep." I handed her a twenty-page breakdown - categorized by project type, partnership history, key personnel. Clean. Precise.

She skimmed the first two pages. "This'll do."

Four o'clock. Alpha Kellan marched in, his scent sharp with urgency.

"San, Eastbridge moved up the schedule. Garrett arrives tomorrow afternoon. Ready?"

Sandra shot up, ears flicking. "They moved it? Well - I've reviewed everything. I'm prepared."

"Good." Kellan's jaw tightened. "Bring someone for on-site support."

Sandra scanned the room. "I'll take Kieran. His German's solid."

"Kieran's still on leave."

Her eyes landed on me. "Jenna. You're coming."

I blinked. "Me? I only speak Italian."

"You'll take notes and fetch coffee." She waved a dismissive hand. "I'll handle the actual translating."

Kellan shot me a skeptical look. "Her?"

"Don't worry, Alpha." Sandra's smile was razor-thin. "She's perfectly capable of assisting."

We hit Eastbridge territory at exactly two o'clock the next day.

"It signals either disrespect or incompetence." His voice dropped to a growl. "Which is it?"

Beside him, his legal director shook his head - a small, disparaging motion.

The deal was dead. Even I could smell it.

Sandra's hands trembled. "Alpha Throne, I'm so sorry - "

He snapped his folder shut. "If this is Nocturne Trading's standard, I'll find another partner."

My fingers hovered over the keyboard.

Two instincts clawed at each other.

One said: Not your problem. You're here for coffee and notes.

The other said: This is the biggest contract of the year. If it falls through, year-end layoffs hit. Bottom-tier wolves like you go first.

Garrett stood to leave. Sandra looked like she might shift from stress right there in the conference room.

I opened my mouth.

German came out.

"Alpha Throne. Give us five more minutes."

Sandra stared at me, wide-eyed. Her jaw dropped.

Garrett paused. He turned.
